name: First-generation biofuels (ethanol, FAME biodiesel)
principle: Ethanol is fermented from starch or sugar crops and biodiesel (FAME) is made by transesterifying vegetable oils and fats. REN21 reports US ethanol of 61.4 billion litres (an all-time high), Brazil 32.5 billion, India 6.35 billion, Indonesian biodiesel 13 billion and total global liquid biofuel output of 175.2 billion litres in 2023.

performance.basis: REN21 states an all-time high; year not stated

performance.metric: life-cycle GHG intensity of first-generation biofuels
performance.unit: % GHG reduction vs petroleum baseline for average US dry-mill corn ethanol (EPA RFS setting, 2023); with indirect land-use change included, a 2025 Transport and Environment study finds global biofuel production emits about 16% MORE CO2 than the fossil fuels replaced
performance.basis: EPA RFS 2023-2025 setting: average US dry-mill corn ethanol has a lifecycle value 39-46% below the petroleum baseline; Transport and Environment-commissioned study (Oct 2025): including ILUC, global biofuels emit about 16% more CO2 than the fossil fuels they replace

source.note: Growth Energy RFS comment (EPA lifecycle values), 10 Feb 2023; agenceurope bulletin 9 Oct 2025 (TE study); read 2026-10-28

limitations: Food-versus-fuel and land-use questions are outside the source
